title: Their view: God concurs by acting on the action and effect, not on the faculty
source_text: XXVII. Itaque longe aliter de concursu illo Dei philosophantur. Primo enim statuunt, Deum cum causis secundis concurrentem & cooperantem non aliquid agere, aut imprimere in ipsam facultatem quae agit, exempli gratia, in voluntatem nostram; sed tantum immediate influere & agere in ipsam actionem, & effectum causae secundae, eamque producere illo ipso momento quo producitur a causa secunda.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore they philosophize far otherwise about that concurrence of God. For first they lay down, that God concurring and cooperating with second causes does not do or imprint something on the faculty itself which acts, for example, on our will; but only immediately flows into and acts on the action itself, and the effect of the second cause, and produces it at that very moment at which it is produced by the second cause.
pass_b_english: They therefore reason about God's concurrence quite differently. First, they hold that when God concurs and cooperates with secondary causes he does not do or impress anything on the faculty that acts, our will, for instance.
He only flows into and acts directly on the action itself and on the effect of the secondary cause, producing it at the very moment the secondary cause produces it.

lemmas.gloss: flow into and act on the action itself

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
